cohort: The study included 898 nulliparous women enrolled with the maternity healthcare service in Orebro County.
finding: The study found an increased risk of fecal incontinence by late pregnancy, and fecal incontinence during pregnancy, obstructed defecation during pregnancy, and concurrent obstructed defecation were associated with an increased prevalence of fecal incontinence 1 year postpartum.
mod_finding: Among women with vaginal delivery, the risk of fecal incontinence and vaginal bulging significantly increased both in late pregnancy and at 1 year postpartum.
